messages.subject: Pairwise comparison with kruskal.test()?
parts:
Hello R-ists,
I'm working on an comparison of noun phrase structures between Kenyan, Singaporean and British English. I've found quite considerable differences in mean noun phrase lengths in one of my datasets, and, now, obviously, I would like to test test whether the differences are significant.

I cannot use Anovas for this purpose, since one of their requirements is not met. The results of a kruskal.test(), though, seem quite promising:

    Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test

data:  LENGTHS by VAR
Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 9.3919, df = 2, p-value = 0.009132

My question is: What function would you use now to get the handy pairwise comparisons yielded by TukeyHSD() in conjunction with Anovas?

I've so far been using the function parwise.wilcox.test() (which I discovered in some R forum for biologists, I believe):

    pairwise.wilcox.test(LENGTHS, VAR, p.adj="holm", exact=F, paired=F)

Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon rank sum test

data:  LENGTHS and VAR

     ea     gb   
gb   0.5790 -    
sing 0.0095 0.0438

This looks quite good, but is this a correct way of doing it? Thank you for your inputs in advance!

Thomas Brunner
